import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import numpy as np

# Read and filter the CSV
df = pd.read_csv('/mnt/uploads/weather.csv', parse_dates=['date'])
london = df.loc[df['city'].eq('London'), ['date', 'temp_c']].groupby('date', as_index=False)['temp_c'].mean().sort_values('date')

# Linear trend fitted to dates expressed as numeric days
x = mdates.date2num(london['date'])
y = london['temp_c'].to_numpy()
coef = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
trend = np.polyval(coef, x)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
ax.plot(london['date'], y, marker='o', label="London temperature")
ax.plot(london['date'], trend, linestyle='--', label='Linear trend')
ax.set_xlabel('Date')
ax.set_ylabel('Temperature (°C)')
ax.set_title("London temperature over time")
ax.legend()
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y-%m-%d'))
fig.autofmt_xdate()
ax.set_ylim(0, max(y.max(), trend.max()) * 1.1)
fig.tight_layout()
